questions.question: In Oracle Database 19c, which server-side service attribute must be set to enable Transparent Application Continuity (TAC) on a database service?

answerOptions.rationale: Setting FAILOVER_TYPE to AUTO enables the database server and driver infrastructure to transparently track session state and inject implicit request boundaries.
FAILOVER_TYPE set to TRANSACTION configures manual Application Continuity, which requires explicit request boundary declarations.
FAILOVER_RESTORE set to LEVEL1 restores preset initial session states, but does not activate the state-tracking infrastructure of TAC on its own.
COMMIT_OUTCOME set to TRUE enables Transaction Guard for outcome verification, which is a prerequisite for Application Continuity but does not enable TAC.

questions.hint: Consider the parameter value that instructs the driver to automatically track state without requiring application code changes.

questions.question: How does the Oracle JDBC Thin driver handle Application Continuity replay when a connection obtained from an XA-capable data source participates in a global/XA transaction?

answerOptions.text: Replay is disabled on that connection until the next request begins.
answerOptions.rationale: Engaging in any global or XA transaction operation disables replay protection on that connection for safety until the connection starts its next request boundary.

answerOptions.text: The global transaction is transparently converted to a local transaction during failover.
answerOptions.rationale: XA transactions involve multi-resource coordination and cannot be converted into local single-resource transactions by the replay driver.

answerOptions.text: Application Continuity replays the transaction standardly across all involved XA resources.
answerOptions.rationale: Application Continuity support for XA data sources only extends to local transactions executed on those connections, not active global transactions.

answerOptions.text: An exception is thrown immediately when calling getXAResource() on the connection.
answerOptions.rationale: Standard XA operations function normally without throwing immediate exceptions, but replay capability is disabled for the duration of the request.

questions.hint: Recall how multi-resource global transaction state affects safety guarantees during failover replay.

questions.question: In IFS Cloud 26R2, which Server Alert Log Category ID creates a system-level AFTER ERROR database trigger upon activation to log database failures?

answerOptions.rationale: Activating the Server Errors category automatically creates an AFTER ERROR trigger in the database to intercept and log all runtime ORA-errors.
Ddl Audit traps schema alteration commands such as CREATE, ALTER, or DROP rather than generic runtime database errors.
Event errors intercepts exceptions encountered during the evaluation or execution of IFS Custom Events and Event Actions.
Debug provides persistent tracing facilities for application developers using explicit internal PL/SQL framework calls.

questions.hint: Look for the category designed specifically to capture transient database ORA-errors raised across application sessions.

questions.question: According to Oracle Maximum Availability Architecture (MAA) reference standards, which tier combines High Availability Clustering, Disaster Recovery, and Backup for mission-critical applications?

answerOptions.rationale: The Gold MAA tier incorporates high availability clustering with database replication for disaster recovery to protect mission-critical business systems.
The Silver tier focuses on high availability clustering and backups for production systems, but lacks a remote disaster recovery site.
The Bronze tier represents single-instance database configurations backed up regularly for non-critical or development workloads.
The Platinum tier targets zero downtime and zero data loss architectures for extreme mission-critical applications beyond standard DR patterns.

questions.hint: Think of the standard MAA progression step between local HA clustering and extreme zero-downtime solutions.

questions.question: What is the primary operational distinction between an Oracle Release Update (RU) and a Release Update Revision (RUR)?

answerOptions.text: RUs contain quarterly cumulative functional and security fixes that increment the minor release, whereas RURs extend an existing RU with security and regression fixes only.
answerOptions.rationale: RUs deliver broad proactive bug fixes and minor release increases, while RURs lock core execution behavior while providing strictly critical security and regression updates.

answerOptions.text: RUs are delivered monthly for production environments, while RURs are released quarterly for non-production environments.
answerOptions.rationale: Both RUs and RURs are delivered on a quarterly cadence by Oracle.

answerOptions.text: RUs increment the revision digit (e.g., 19.11.0 to 19.11.1), while RURs increment the minor release version (e.g., 19.3.0 to 19.4.0).
answerOptions.rationale: Applying an RU increments the minor release version digit, whereas applying an RUR increments the revision digit.

answerOptions.text: RURs introduce brand-new application features, whereas RUs strictly contain security patches.
answerOptions.rationale: RUs contain proactive functional enhancements and security fixes, whereas RURs contain no new functional features.

questions.hint: Identify which patch maintenance strategy targets stability-focused systems by limiting functional scope changes.

questions.question: Which Oracle database background process is responsible for flushing in-memory statistics from the SGA into Automatic Workload Repository (AWR) tables in SYSAUX?

answerOptions.rationale: The Memory Monitor (MMON) background process handles the periodic flushing of active session history and SGA performance statistics to the AWR repository.
ONS (Oracle Notification Service) is a communications infrastructure used for Fast Application Notification events, not database performance sampling.
PMON cleans up failed user process resources and manages background process recovery.
CKPT updates data file headers and signals the database writer during checkpoints, but does not flush performance telemetry to AWR.

questions.hint: Identify the background process focused on memory statistics collection and repository maintenance.

questions.question: When configuring a database service for Application Continuity, what value is assigned to FAILOVER_RESTORE when FAILOVER_TYPE is set to AUTO?

answerOptions.rationale: Setting FAILOVER_TYPE to AUTO automatically sets FAILOVER_RESTORE to AUTO, enforcing session initial state restoration.
LEVEL1 is used for manual Application Continuity configurations where FAILOVER_TYPE is set to TRANSACTION.
NONE is the default value when FAILOVER_RESTORE is unconfigured, but it is overridden when FAILOVER_TYPE is set to AUTO.
MANUAL is not a valid attribute setting for the FAILOVER_RESTORE service parameter.

questions.hint: The value of this restore attribute automatically inherits the setting mode specified for the failover type.

questions.question: To retain mutable function results (such as SYSDATE or SYS_GUID) during Application Continuity replay, what SQL privilege must a DBA grant to the application database user?

answerOptions.text: KEEP privilege (e.g., KEEP DATE TIME, KEEP SYSGUID)
answerOptions.rationale: DBAs grant KEEP privileges to ensure Application Continuity can save and restore mutable function results for code executed by custom or app users.
DBMS_REPLAY is part of Database Replay for database workload testing, not the Application Continuity driver runtime state retention.
ALTER SESSION permits session-level parameter adjustments, but does not grant authority to retain mutable function values during replay.
FLASHBACK privileges allow querying historical table data, but do not control mutable function outcome retention in JDBC replay.

questions.hint: Think of the grant syntax keyword specifically intended to preserve or keep function return values consistent.

questions.question: To enforce a strict Recovery Point Objective of zero ($RPO = 0$) in an Oracle Data Guard architecture, which redo transport mode must be enabled on the primary database?

answerOptions.rationale: Synchronous transport ensures transaction commits on the primary are held until the redo data is written to standby redo logs on the remote site, preventing data loss.
Asynchronous transport allows the primary database to commit transactions without waiting for standby acknowledgment, leaving a potential data loss window.
Maximum Performance protection mode utilizes asynchronous redo transport, which prioritizes primary performance over zero data loss.
Fast-Start Failover affects automated recovery time (RTO), but does not define the underlying redo log transport synchronization mode.

questions.hint: Consider how transaction commits must wait for network acknowledgment from standby redo logs.

questions.question: Which explicit APIs are provided by the oracle.jdbc.OracleConnection interface to allow Java applications to declare request boundaries for memory purging and replay safety?

answerOptions.rationale: The beginRequest and endRequest methods explicitly mark units of work, enabling the JDBC Replay Driver to purge call history and manage memory efficiently.
These are non-existent or standard transaction demarcations, not the explicit Application Continuity request boundary APIs.
Dynamic replay control APIs are located on replay connection proxies, but do not define explicit request boundary markers.
Connection checkout and checkin are connection pool lifecycle operations rather than methods on the OracleConnection interface.

questions.hint: Look for methods named directly after opening and closing a request boundary.

questions.question: Starting with Oracle Database Release 12.1.0.2, which set of parameters is explicitly recommended in the JDBC thin driver connection URL to improve connection acquisition during failover and planned outages?

answerOptions.rationale: These parameters optimize network connection acquisition timing across SCAN listeners and database host VIPs during runtime and failover events.
These settings govern connection pool memory and transaction autocommit behavior rather than network failover transport retries.
Connecting by SID or INSTANCE_NAME is deprecated for high availability and does not direct connections to known good instances during failover.
This syntax represents legacy TAF (Transparent Application Failover) configuration parameters rather than modern JDBC Thin Net Services parameters.

questions.hint: Focus on parameters controlling client-side socket connection timeouts and retry attempts.

questions.question: According to the IFS Cloud 25R1 technical documentation for Oracle 19c Enterprise Edition options, what is the official support status of Oracle Database Vault?

answerOptions.rationale: The official IFS Cloud 25R1 matrix specifically marks Oracle Database Vault as 'Not tested/verified for IFS Cloud' (N).

answerOptions.text: Fully supported and verified on IFS Applications 10 and IFS Cloud
answerOptions.rationale: Active Data Guard, Advanced Security, and In-Memory are listed as verified, but Database Vault is explicitly marked as untested.
Standard Edition 2 does not include enterprise options like Database Vault, nor is it listed as supported for Database Vault in IFS matrices.
Database Vault is an optional security component and is not mandated or verified in standard IFS deployment matrices.

questions.hint: Check the verification table status for Database Vault in contrast to Active Data Guard or Advanced Security.
